literal: Hand-spear at elephant having thrown, he who comes body-spear having pulled out, will smile.
translation: The warrior who threw his spear at an elephant and comes looking for another, pulls out a spear pierced in his own chest and smiles.
modern: தன் கையிலிருந்த வேலை எதிரியின் யானை மீது வீசிவிட்டு, வேறு ஆயுதம் தேடி வருபவன், தன் மார்பில் தைத்திருக்கும் வேலைக் கண்டு அதனைப் பிடுங்கி மகிழ்ந்து சிரிப்பான்.
explanation: This couplet vividly illustrates the fearless spirit of a true warrior. In the heat of battle, a soldier hurls his spear at a charging elephant and is left unarmed. Looking for another weapon to continue fighting, he finds a spear lodged in his own chest, pulls it out, and smiles in triumph. The word 'நகும்' (smiles) captures his sheer joy in finding a weapon, completely ignoring the pain of his wound.
